subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the length of the perpendicular drawn from the point (−2, −3) to the straight line 5x − 2y + 4 = 0.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 11, book p.141. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. DEGENERATE AS PRINTED, AND AUTHORED THAT WAY: the stem is reproduced exactly as the book prints it, and with those numbers 5(−2) − 2(−3) + 4 = −10 + 6 + 4 = 0, so the point lies ON the line and the perpendicular distance is 0. That is the correct answer to the question as printed, not a defect in this card, and it has NOT been repaired into a non-zero distance by changing a coefficient or a coordinate. Whether the book intended a different constant term cannot be known from the stem alone, so nothing has been guessed. The answer therefore teaches the case a student meets often on a board paper: a zero numerator is the test for a point lying on a line, and 0 is a valid distance. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for the formula with its modulus and square root written correctly, and the second for the substitution and the conclusion; a candidate who writes the formula correctly still earns the first mark whatever the numerator turns out to be. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say the distance formula, then say what a zero numerator tells you.

steps.label: Write the distance formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two things carry marks in this formula and both are easy to drop: the modulus on top and the square root below.
steps.memory_tip: Distance = |line at the point| divided by √(a² + b²). Modulus on top, square root below.

recall.must_convey: That the perpendicular distance formula |ax₁ + by₁ + c| / √(a² + b²) is written, with a = 5, b = −2, c = 4.

steps.why: √(a² + b²) is the length of the vector (a, b) at right angles to the line, and dividing by it turns the raw value ax₁ + by₁ + c into a true length.
common_mistakes: Writing a² + b² without the square root.

steps.label: Substitute and read the distance
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The numerator comes out 0 here. That is not a slip: it says P satisfies the equation of the line, so P is a point of the line itself and there is no gap to measure.
steps.memory_tip: A zero numerator is the test for a point lying on a line. Its distance is then 0, and 0 is a real answer.

steps.why: The foot of the perpendicular from P is the nearest point of the line to P. When P is already a point of the line, that nearest point is P itself, so the perpendicular has length 0.
